ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles 2, 4, 5, 5-2, and 6 of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information; Article 5-7 and related provisions of the Enforcement Decree thereof; the Financial Services Commission Regulations on Financial Transaction Reporting and Monitoring; the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Owner Identification Guide; and Articles 17-2 and 174 of the Commercial Act governing trade-name registration and corporate existence. The Korean registry does not maintain a public UBO list; beneficial ownership data is collected by regulated financial institutions and reported to KoFIU for government-only supervisory and law-enforcement access.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registration Division of the competent district court having territorial jurisdiction over the Yuhan Hoesa head office, e.g., Seoul Central District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: issue the registry certificate, have the certifying officer signature authenticated by a Korean notary, and obtain an apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular Legalization path solely for non-Hague destination states: issue the certificate, certify the signer, obtain MOFA legalization, and then obtain legalization from the destination state consulate or embassy in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternative routes and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Current Corporate Registry Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office and the competent district court of registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: obtain the certified current corporate registry extract, notarize the issuing officer signature, then apply for an apostille at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular Legalization path for non-Apostille destinations: notarization, MOFA legalization, then legalization by the destination state diplomatic mission in Korea. The two authentication methods are parallel and mutually exclusive; they cannot be used in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation, bank account opening, and local registered agent appointment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the founding shareholder or ultimate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: execute the resolution and power of attorney before a Korean notary, then submit to the Apostille Section of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular Legalization path solely for non-Apostille destination states: notarize, obtain MOFA legalization, and then obtain consular legalization from the destination country mission in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are exclusive alternatives and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jang-gwan) of Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders and the Korean notary public certifying incorporation under Article 178 of the Commercial Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize the articles and obtain an apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular Legalization path for non-Hague states: notarize, MOFA legalization, then destination state consular legalization in Korea. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; do not perform both sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a reputable financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution holding the deposit or business account of the beneficial owner and ultimate parent, such as a Korean commercial bank or international correspondent bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: bank officer signature certified by a Korean notary, then apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular Legalization path solely for non-Apostille states: bank officer acknowledgment, Korean notarization, MOFA legalization, then consular legalization at the destination state embassy or consulate in Korea. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive routes and must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be completed against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit suspicious transaction report database thresholds, the domestic consolidated list of designated individuals and entities, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the U.K. HM Treasury sanctions list, and Interpol Red Notice and adverse media databases. The compliance program must apply a risk-based approach to every natural person owning or controlling 25% or more of the Yuhan Hoesa or otherwise exercising de facto control, including directors, senior managers, trustees, and nominee shareholders. PEP screening must cover domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members, known close associates, and companies controlled by them. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP, politically exposed legal person, or jurisdiction under FATF monitoring; the partner must document source of funds, purpose of the container leasing business, and expected transactional volume. Sanctions screening shall be performed at onboarding, at formation, and continuously on every registry, banking, or shareholding event using fuzzy-name and alias normalization; any positive hit must be escalated to KoFIU under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO, iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Articles 17-2 and 174 of the Commercial Act, a Yuhan Hoesa must have a trade name distinguishable from existing registered trade names for the same or similar business purpose. The registered name may be in a foreign language, but the court registry requires a Hangul transliteration and the statutory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive element; (2) a descriptive business purpose element such as container leasing; (3) the legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and (4) no prohibited token without prior ministerial approval. Phonetic transliteration must be faithful to the Korean alphabet, and the English translation used in contracts and banking must match the registered Hangul transliteration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registration examiner rejects or requests correction of the proposed trade name, the applicant must obtain the written reasons from the registry examiner within three business days. The applicant may then file an objection with the competent district court under Article 295 of the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, attaching a corrected name proposal, the original clearance receipt, and any ministerial no-objection letter required for a sensitive token. The court reviews the administrative decision and may either sanction the registration or order the applicant to amend the articles. There is no right to extend the 30-day reservation window; the applicant should prepare to reapply immediately with a new name variation, thereby preserving the incorporation timetable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or shared business-center address may be accepted for corporate registration if a genuine service agreement exists and the service provider has a verifiable physical presence in Korea. However, for a container-leasing entity in ISIC 5229, the National Tax Service and commercial banks will scrutinize whether the registered address corresponds to actual management functions, asset custody, and contractual service performance. A standalone commercial mailbox or virtual office without personnel, board meeting facilities, or asset records is likely to be rejected by banks for account opening and may trigger a deemed lack of commercial substance for VAT refunds and foreign investment protection. If a virtual office is used, the company must appoint a local registered agent, maintain physical evidence of managerial acts, and disclose the service arrangement to the tax registration office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to elevated: unannounced on-site inspection risk is quantified at approximately 35% for a first-year company with a physical office, and 65% for a company with only a virtual office or which reports no employees in Korea. The inspection checklist used by municipal tax authorities and registry officers includes: written lease agreement, visible company signboard, business books and container lease ledger, board minutes, bank statements, asset inspection records, and evidence that the registered address is not merely a forwarding agency. The absence of any of these indicators materially increases the likelihood of a formal on-site audit and may delay issuance of a business registration certificate.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent district court registration office and municipal local tax authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Registration License Tax Act and rules of court fees; estimated for zero to modest authorized capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Trade-name clearance and UBO due diligence review, including sanctions/PEP screening and corporate registry document verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean law firm / corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border Korean entity formation and AML due diligence packages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association, board resolution, and power of attorney by a Korean notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary fee schedule of the Korean Notary Association

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization processing fees, excluding destination embassy and courier fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official MOFA fee schedule and consular fee tariffs, not including third-party courier services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter and initial corporate bank account on-boarding support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank and external legal counsel in Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank service fee tariff and prevailing market benchmark for account-opening assistance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office or licensed business-center virtual office arrangement for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed office service provider in Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing commercial market rate for a physical or virtual office lease with reception services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual prevailing market benchmark for Korean corporate secretarial and registered agent services

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, as amended, particularly Articles 288 through 317 on incorporation of a stock company and limited liability company, Articles 362 through 370 on the board of directors, Article 383 on the number of directors, Article 388 on director remuneration, and Article 397 on the duty of loyalty; Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident shareholders; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for foreign investment notifications; and the Framework Act on the Management of Concessions for administrative fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court, operating through the Korean Internet Registration Office (I-Plus) under the Administration of Courts; post-registration tax filings are handled by the local National Tax Service District Tax Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporate Registration (incorporation registration) filed together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, certificate of deposit of subscription price, statement of acceptance by directors, and minutes of the incorporators meeting and first board meeting.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists under the Commercial Act, but the entire subscribed capital must be deposited and blocked in a capital subscription escrow account at a Korean bank before the court will register the company. For an intermodal container leasing company, a paid-in capital of KRW 100,000,000 is recommended to establish commercial creditworthiness. The state filing burden consists of registration tax of 0.4 percent of subscribed capital, an education surtax of 20 percent of the registration tax, and a court collection fee; for the recommended KRW 100,000,000 capital subscription, the aggregate official fee is approximately USD 650.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators and sole initial shareholder of Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company to be organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, hereby subscribe to the entire authorized share capital of the Company, consisting of 10,000 ordinary shares with par value of KRW 10,000 each, for an aggregate subscription price of KRW 100,000,000 (the Initial Capital). RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Initial Capital shall be fully paid by wire transfer into a capital subscription escrow account maintained by the Companys appointed bank in the Republic of Korea, and that no share certificate shall be physically issued and no repayment of subscription price shall be made until the court registration of the Company is completed and a certificate of corporate registration is obtained. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be established at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation within the registration jurisdiction of the Seoul Central District Court, and that the Articles of Incorporation, as notarized, are hereby approved and adopted as the conclusive instrument of governance of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following banks, namely the bank designated by the directors at this meeting, are authorized to open deposit, operating, foreign currency, and settlement accounts on behalf of the Company and to accept funds from all lawful sources; the signature authority on all such accounts shall be vested jointly in the representative director and the chief financial officer or any two directors as designated from time to time by the board. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors named in the appointment minutes are hereby appointed as representative director, inside director, and auditor, each to hold office for the statutory term, and that no officer shall receive compensation unless approved by the general meeting of shareholders. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors are authorized to execute all contracts, leases, insurance policies, tax registrations, and governmental applications necessary to conduct intermodal ISO shipping container fleet asset leasing, including but not limited to container depot agreements, master lease agreements, customs-bonded facility registrations, and financing documents, and to engage counsel and agents for the completion of corporate registration with the competent court and the National Tax Service. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the corporate seal of the Company shall be adopted in the form submitted to the board, and the representative director is authorized to register the seal impression with the competent registry office and to use such seal in all official filings and commercial documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Clearance, Foreign Investment Pre-Review, and Registered Office Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registry Office through the Internet Registration Office (I-Plus), the receiving foreign-exchange bank, and Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency for non-resident investors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an official name search on the Internet Registration Office to ensure that the proposed Korean corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company in the same business category, and include the auxiliary English name Yuhan Hoesa. If any shareholder is a non-resident or foreign enterprise, file a foreign investment notification with the receiving bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and if investment incentives are desired, obtain a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate from KOTRA or the designated foreign-exchange bank. Confirm that the proposed registered office and any container depot location have lawful land use under the National Land Planning and Utilization Act and that the landlord has consented to the registration of the corporate office. This pre-review reduces the risk of registry suspension during the court filing stage.
required_dossiers: Corporate name search result
Passport or corporate certificate of identification of all shareholders, with apostille if foreign
Foreign investment notification certificate or foreign exchange bank receipt
Registered office lease agreement or landlord consent letter
Proposed Articles of Incorporation draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate name is rejected or queried, submit a written request for reconsideration to the Registration Division and provide an alternative name list; if the foreign investment notification is questioned, supplement the beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declaration to the receiving bank within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Escrow Account Opening and Share Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated commercial bank in the Republic of Korea authorized to hold capital subscription escrow deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital subscription account in the name of the company with a licensed commercial bank and deposit the full subscription price of KRW 100,000,000. The bank will issue a certificate of receipt of paid-in capital stating the deposit date, account number, subscriber identity, and aggregate amount. The funds must remain blocked until the court registration of incorporation is completed; the bank may require beneficial ownership declarations and source-of-funds evidence under anti-money laundering obligations. After registration, the bank releases the funds to the company operating account upon presentation of the certificate of corporate registration.
required_dossiers: Application for capital subscription account
Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Identification documents and beneficial ownership declaration of all subscribers
Certificate of foreign investment notification, if applicable
Source-of-funds statement from each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises an anti-money laundering query, supply revised organizational charts, beneficial owner identification, and source-of-funds ledgers within five business days; any correction to the deposited amount must be made before the notarization step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Execution by Capital Subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Law notary public with jurisdiction over the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an incorporators meeting or obtain unanimous written consent to the final Korean-language Articles of Incorporation. The Articles must include the corporate name, business purpose covering intermodal ISO container fleet leasing, depot operation if authorized, and related logistics support, the registered office address, authorized share capital, directors seats, and fiscal year. Every incorporator or authorized attorney must sign before the notary, and the notary must certify the signatures and the legality of the Articles under the Commercial Act. Foreign signatories must present notarized and apostilled powers of attorney with certified Korean translation. The notary then stamps the Articles and returns certified copies for court filing.
required_dossiers: Final Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
Notarized and apostilled power of attorney, if signed by proxy
Certificate of deposit of subscription price
Capital subscribers identification documents and tax numbers
Record of incorporators consent or meeting minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect, pass a written amendment resolution, reprint the signature pages, and re-notarize; if a subscriber refuses to sign, adjust the capital subscription amount, return or supplement escrow funds, and restate the share schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration of Incorporation and Issuance of Corporate Seal Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the competent District Court, such as the Seoul Central District Court, via the Internet Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application with the court registration division, attaching the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the banks certificate of capital deposit, subscribers statements, directors written acceptances, and the first board appointment minutes. The registration officer examines the formal legal compliance and enters the company into the commercial register. Upon approval, the court issues the certificate of corporate registration, certified register extracts, and a seal certificate. The company is legally formed as of the registration date. The representative director must then register the corporate seal impression and may begin pre-operational contracts, but no public business may be conducted before tax registration is completed.
required_dossiers: Application for corporate registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of deposit of subscription price
Statement of acceptance signed by each director
Minutes of incorporators meeting and first board meeting
Corporate seal impression certificate and seal registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a suspension or request for correction, file a written explanation and supplemental documents within fourteen days; if the capital amount changes, pay the additional registration tax and re-file within the same cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Post-Incorporation Regulatory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Tax Service District Tax Office with jurisdiction over the registered office, and the relevant municipal or port licensing office if a container depot is operated
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of court registration, complete the business registration application to obtain the business registration certificate and corporate taxpayer number. Register for value-added tax, corporate income tax, electronic tax invoices, and withholding tax. If employees are hired, register each worker with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance. If the company will operate a container yard or depot, file the applicable logistics facility report with the local government and coordinate with the Korea Customs Service for any customs-bonded container storage authorization. The first corporate tax return should be prepared with audited opening balance sheet data.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration
Corporate seal certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Proof of registered office ownership or lease
Opening balance sheet and capital escrow release confirmation
Directors identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests a desk audit or additional documents, deliver the requested ledger and source documents within ten business days; if a municipal logistics facility permit is suspended, cure the land-use or fire-safety deficiency and reapply within the statutory cure period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport for logistics facility regulation, local municipal government within the Si/Gun/Gu jurisdiction, Korea Customs Service for bonded container operations, and the National Fire Agency for civil defense and fire safety clearances.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Container Depot / Logistics Facility Operation Report under the Logistics Facilities Development and Operation Act, and if the depot is within a harbor area, a Container Terminal Occupation and Use Permit under the Harbor Area Usage and Development Act; a pure financial container leasing operation without physical storage requires no separate industrial operating license beyond ordinary business registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, with technical review by the Korea Environment Institute and local environmental protection authorities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D/E Environmental Registration or Exempt by classification; a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not required for a pure intermodal container leasing and depot operation without repair, painting, degreasing, or chemical handling. A full EIA or small-scale EIA is triggered only if the operator introduces container repair, abrasive blasting, spray painting, chemical cleaning, or any activity exceeding the thresholds in the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For pure container leasing and stacking, no process wastewater or volatile organic compound emissions are expected, but stormwater runoff must be managed in accordance with the Water Environment Conservation Act. If container washing, painting, degreasing, or VOC-emitting operations are introduced, the operator must install pollution prevention equipment and comply with effluent limits such as BOD of 40 mg/L or less, COD of 40 mg/L or less, suspended solids of 40 mg/L or less, T-N of 60 mg/L or less, and T-P of 8 mg/L or less, with hazardous waste manifests under the Wastes Control Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the office and container depot issued by the local fire department under the Fire Prevention and Safety Control of Dangerous Goods Act; civil defense shelter designation and emergency evacuation plan approved through the local civil defense authority; structural load inspection certificate for any crane, racking, or stacking system; and occupational safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act covering forklift operator licenses, stack stability, traffic management, and a certified workplace safety plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, electronic portal Home Tax Service at www.hometax.go.kr; export customs matters are administered by Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance portal at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must appoint a domestic tax representative recognised by the NTS, file the official Business Registration Application in the prescribed NTS form through Home Tax Service or at the competent district tax office, and submit statutory attachments comprising certificate of incorporation, foreign registration and corporate existence documentation, constitutional documents, domestic business office or lease evidence, and a power of attorney appointing the tax representative. After verification, the NTS assigns a ten-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as the unified TIN, VAT registration number, and corporate income tax identifier. A domestic Yuhan Hoesa completes the same BRN procedure within twenty days of business commencement. The entity must additionally register as a trading entity in UNI-PASS with the same BRN before making export declarations. The BRN certificate is retrievable electronically through Home Tax Service and is the sole statutory tax identity credential for indirect tax transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea has no US-style check-the-box election. A Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate taxation on worldwide income, and no hybrid mismatch pass-through election is available for a Korean incorporated entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act and its Presidential Enforcement Decree
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Every business operator, including a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa, must complete VAT registration before commencing taxable activity. The mandatory economic turnover threshold distinguishing general VAT taxpayers from simplified taxable persons is annual taxable supplies exceeding KRW 80,000,000 in the preceding calendar year; an entity supplying FCL container leasing services with expected consideration above that threshold must register as a general VAT taxpayer, issue standard tax invoices, and file regular VAT returns. In all cases, a newly incorporated Yuhan Hoesa must file the Business Registration Application within 20 days of business commencement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) must be issued for B2B supplies and transmitted through Home Tax Service or an NTS-approved electronic service provider no later than the day following the supply date. The NTS receives and cross-matches e-tax invoice data in real time to validate input VAT claims. For B2C transactions, the mandatory KCash Cash Receipt System must issue cash receipts. There is no separate anti-fraud digital stamping system in the Mexican or Italian sense; the anti-fraud mechanism is the mandatory real-time transmission to NTS, electronic invoice matching, periodic VAT reconciliation, and cash receipt surveillance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, zero-rating applies to goods that are actually exported under a customs export declaration. For cross-border FCL box container leasing, zero-rating is available if the container lease is characterised as an exported service or as an export of goods depending on the contractual and physical facts. The statutory criteria require that the supply is made to a non-resident lessee, the container is used outside Korea or in international shipping, the risk and benefit of the lease are offshore, and the consideration is paid in foreign currency. The taxpayer must retain complete transactional, movement, and foreign-exchange evidence to prove that the benefit of the supply is realised outside the Korean VAT territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) issued by Korea Customs Service showing the container export, export date, and classification
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill evidencing the international movement and foreign destination or offshore use of the leased container
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Receipt Confirmation issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank proving receipt of foreign-currency lease consideration
Container leasing agreement and ISO container identification list demonstrating the foreign lessee, lease term, and offshore utilisation
Commercial invoice for the lease rental or export value prepared in foreign currency
Packing list or cargo manifest cross-referencing container numbers with the export declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may perform in-depth zero-rating audits and retrospectively disallow the 0% rate if the customs export declaration, Bill of Lading, lease documentation, or foreign-currency repatriation evidence is absent, inconsistent, or fabricated. Disallowed zero-rating is clawed back by assessing the standard 10% VAT on the supply value, denying associated input VAT refunds, and applying statutory imputed additional taxes for non-issuance, false e-tax invoices, underreporting, and late filing. Export proceeds must be repatriated within 180 days under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; failure to timely repatriate without a lawful extension can itself invalidate the zero-rating treatment. Fraudulent zero-rating claims may be referred for criminal prosecution under the Framework Act on Taxes and the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, with fines and imprisonment exposure in addition to full VAT recovery, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the foreign exchange information system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Presidential Decree
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South Korean won (KRW) is convertible for current-account transactions, including merchanting, services, and ordinary lease payments, subject to submission of underlying trade or transaction documents through a licensed foreign-exchange bank. Capital-account convertibility is more constrained: foreign direct investment requires a notification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, typically processed through KOTRA or an authorized bank, while portfolio investments and external borrowings require prior declaration or approval. Profit remittance and liquidation proceeds are generally free once taxes are cleared, but each payment must be documented using statutory purpose codes and validated by a designated foreign-exchange bank. Korean residents, including domestic LLCs, may maintain foreign-currency accounts, but spending within Korea is mandatory in KRW; non-resident KRW accounts remain highly restricted and cannot be used for capital transactions absent licensed bank intermediation. Major practical hurdles include the strict documentary audit trail for cross-border rental income, the requirement to match foreign-currency receipts to export declarations or service invoices, and an anti-abuse scrutiny of corporate structures backed by foreign shareholders. The BOK and MOEF jointly enforce capital-flow management measures, ensuring that all outward remittances of dividends or capital reduce the entity's registered investment amount and must be supported by audited financial statements and a certificate of investment completion. The overall regime is liberal for trade and leasing, but the Korean user of an offshore fintech EMI cannot access onshore KRW clearing; all local payment and collection must transit a regulated Korean bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export and cross-border service proceeds must be collected within 15 months of the export declaration or shipment date, unless extended by the foreign-exchange bank. Exporters may hold the proceeds in a domestic foreign-currency account or deliver them to a licensed foreign-exchange bank; there is no mandatory percentage conversion for ordinary trade proceeds, but any conversion to KRW must be executed through a licensed bank and reported using the appropriate export settlement code. For leasing income from intermodal containers, the rental invoices and equipment sub-headers must demonstrate a valid service export so that the remittance can be classified as current-account earnings and not as an unapproved capital inflow.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and not legally viable for onshore KRW operations. An offshore digital EMI, even if licensed in Singapore, the EU, or the UK, is not permitted to open KRW clearing accounts or provide local payment rails in South Korea. Korean banking law requires all inbound and outbound KRW flows to be settled through domestic licensed banks, and a foreign LLC entity cannot hold a virtual account without a real bank partnership. The EMI can only serve as a technical layer for foreign-currency collection, but it cannot satisfy capital verification, tax withholding, or statutory FX reporting obligations. Therefore, the treasury blueprint must designate a Korean Tier-1 commercial bank as the primary settlement rail and may use EMIs merely for incidental foreign-currency receivables if the EMI has a licensed Korean bank sponsor; in practice, no such arrangement is available on a compliant basis.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: All statutory directors of the Korean entity must appear in person at a domestic branch of the designated foreign-exchange bank for a compliance interview before any account is activated. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by Korean banks for a business entity, although the foreign exchange bank may conduct a videoconference after the initial physical visit. The signature card, corporate seal, and foreign-investor registration certificate must be authenticated in-branch. If a director is not available to travel, a written power of attorney with apostilled notarization must be presented, but the designated responsible party in Korea must still attend a physical interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or director appears on sanctioned-party screening or is connected to a high-risk jurisdiction, causing the bank compliance committee to request enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport and visa, residence card, a detailed curriculum vitae, a source-of-funds statement, a source-of-wealth report, utility bills, tax transcripts from the previous five years, bank references, and a signed declaration that no sanctioned entity has a beneficial interest

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Artificial beneficial-ownership chain obscuring the true controllers of the container leasing entity, tripping the bank's Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) filing threshold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified corporate organizational chart, share register, copy of the articles of incorporation, beneficial-ownership declaration under Korean Real Name Financial Transactions Act, trust deeds or nominee agreements, and sworn statutory declarations from each intermediate holding company

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lease and rental remittances from container usage are suspected to be disguised trade financing, especially when the same container is chartered to multiple foreign parties without a clear trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master high-seas container lease agreements, equipment interchange reports, telex release documents, container positioning/telematics logs, voyage schedules, port invoices, cargo manifests, and a web portal showing continuous tracking plus reconciliation of rental invoices to the cash flow

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Account activity indicates potential round-tripping with foreign subsidiaries and repeated inbound and outbound wires not aligned with the declared operating scope
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany service agreements, proof of arm's-length pricing, transfer pricing documentation, board minutes approving each wire, audited financial statements, customs declarations for the equipment, and a detailed liquidity projection explaining the timing and purpose of each remittance

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections into the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must be processed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act via a KOTRA-backed notification form or through an authorized bank with FDI declaration capability. The funds must be remitted through a licensed foreign-exchange bank into a dedicated capital injection escrow account designated as 'Foreign Investment Capital Account'; the bank will verify the currency purchase, issue a certificate of foreign exchange purchase or a foreign investment registration certificate, and record the inward remittance with the Foreign Exchange Information Network. The company must subsequently file an investment determination report, and the bank will conduct a capital verification based on the actual inward transfer before the capital account can be converted into a general operating account. The wiring protocol must include the correct FX purpose code (e.g., 'FDI into a Korean corporation'), a clear reference to the foreign investment declaration number, and a matching KRW equivalent at the BOK base rate. No EB-5 or quasi-equity parking is permissible; all equity must be admitted as fully paid.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the container leasing business should be executed primarily via SWIFT MT103 for rental, insurance, maintenance, and management fees to global clients and contractors. For high-value chassis or container purchases and repair overhauls, a Commercial Letter of Credit is recommended, using a standard UCP600 LC with the Korean bank as issuing bank and the offshore supplier as beneficiary. Documentary collections are acceptable for low-value repair parts where prudent control is limited. Domestic ACH debits may be used for port fees, container yard handling, and utility settling in KRW, but every international payment must carry a valid Import/Export or Leasing Service invoice and a proper FX payment classification. Trade file routing should include the bank's assigned treasury reference so that merchanting rentals are not misclassified as capital outflows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instryments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign-exchange bank, supported by signed lease agreements or container purchase contracts
Onshore foreign-currency options (including European-style products) for hedging lease receivables where the base currency is USD or EUR and the functional currency is KRW
Cross-currency swaps for matching the USD/rental assets with KRW operating liabilities, available only through a licensed bank with a documented underlying exposure
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are prohibited for Korean residents; therefore only onshore hedging instruments using the BOK KRW fixing are permitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic tax filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after close of the fiscal year (for 31 December year-end: on or before 31 March of the following year; a one-month extension to 30 April applies if a tax preparer submits a final return request)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If not filed, additional tax of 20% of the unreported corporate tax; understatement triggers 10% penalty tax; overdue tax accrues daily late payment interest at 0.022% from the due date. NTS may seize assets after one month of delinquency and may cancel the taxpayer's business registration if non-filing continues; repeated delinquencies can lead to criminal indictment and court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (Si/Gun/Gu) via NTS HomeTax with corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as national corporate income tax: within 3 months after fiscal year end (by 31 March; extended to 30 April)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge penalties: 20% failure-to-file penalty, 10% understatement penalty, and 0.022% daily delay interest. Local tax authorities may issue compulsory collection orders and seize property if unpaid after the statutory due date.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report of Independent Certified Public Accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System (DART); electronic copy to National Tax Service (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the annual general meeting of members, which must be held within 3 months after fiscal year close (by 31 March); the audit report is filed with DART within 14 days after the general meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If an audit-subject company does not file the audit report within the statutory deadline, the Securities and Futures Commission may impose an administrative fine up to KRW 30 million, require a corrective audit at company expense, and the financial statements may lose evidentiary tax value; sustained failure may lead to prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or a designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the fiscal year-end (by 30 January for a calendar-year entity); transfers of foreign-invested equity are separately reportable within 30 days of transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a negligence fine up to KRW 5 million; undeclared foreign investment can lose its registration status and with it tax exemptions, dividend remittance guarantees, and investment incentives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of Annual Financial Statements at General Meeting of Members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's corporate governance bodies (Board of Directors and General Meeting of Members); no external governmental fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of each fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors jointly and severally liable for damages caused by failure to approve financial statements; persistent failure to convene the meeting may permit a court to dissolve the company on application of a shareholder or creditor.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory if the Yuhan Hoesa: (a) has total assets of at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million) at the end of the preceding fiscal year; (b) has total assets of at least KRW 2 billion and falls within the Presidential Decree category of companies, for example, a company in which foreign investors hold at least 30% of the voting equity or whose equity interests are held by 100 or more persons; (c) is engaged in a financial, credit-specialized, or special-law regulated business requiring audit; or (d) voluntarily opts into statutory audit by shareholder resolution. For container-box leasing, revenue alone does not create a separate turnover trigger, and headcount does not independently trigger external audit; however, if the container fleet entity is a material subsidiary of a parent required to prepare consolidated Korean IFRS financial statements, the parent audit will include the entity, and consolidation may make K-IFRS and audit compulsory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean IFRS (K-IFRS) is mandatory for audit-subject companies; non-listed, non-audit-subject entities may apply Korean Accounting Standards (K-GAAP) or Korean SME Accounting Standards, which substantively align with IFRS for SMEs; accounting frameworks must be applied consistently and disclosed in the financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not require a separate annual UBO filing on a public register for a closed Yuhan Hoesa, but the company has a continuous statutory obligation to maintain an accurate register of members showing each member's name, address, equity interest, and transfer history. Share transfers to foreign nationals or non-residents must be reported to MOTIE via KOTRA within 30 days of the transfer. A foreign-invested company must file an annual foreign investment status report within 30 days after each fiscal year end. For AML/CDD purposes, the ultimate beneficial owner of any member holding directly or indirectly a controlling equity interest must be identified and recorded on-site, with a risk-based refresh cycle appropriate for a low-risk standard container-leasing file; changes in beneficial ownership are recorded when they occur. Non-compliance with foreign investment and AML reporting obligations triggers fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and CFT regulations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Meetings and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,500 - US$7,000 per year for registered office at a domestic business address, resident company secretary, and statutory agent services in Korea; premium Seoul locations may range up to US$12,000.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$10,000 - US$45,000 per audit engagement for a container-leasing LLC, depending on container fleet asset value, number of lease contracts, related-party disclosures, consolidation involvement, and CPA firm tier.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% for taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% for income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 21% for income between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion; 24% for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax holidays available for qualifying foreign-invested high-tech businesses under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (RSTA); Free Economic Zone (FEZ) incentives include 100% corporate tax exemption for 3 years and 50% reduction for 2 years for qualifying new businesses; R&D tax credits up to 30-50% of qualifying R&D expenditures; no patent box regime, but foreign-source income exemption for qualifying overseas business establishments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return – Form No. 2 (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서) filed via HomeTax System (홈택스, www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year; for fiscal year ending December 31, filing due by March 31; six-month extension available upon application for foreign-invested companies under the Framework Act on International Taxation Coordination

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the corporate registration number, head office address, representative director details, and business commencement date. For a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa, ensure the foreign shareholder's tax identification number (TIN) and country of residence are disclosed to trigger treaty withholding analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial Statement Reconciliation (Income Statement and Balance Sheet)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report financial statements prepared under K-IFRS. Reconcile book income to taxable income by adding non-deductible expenses (e.g., entertainment expenses exceeding statutory limits, penalties, certain intercompany royalties) and deducting non-taxable income (e.g., dividends received under the holding company exemption). Cross-border container leasing income must be allocated based on the situs of the leased assets and the OECD Authorized OECD Approach for permanent establishment attribution.

For a Korean domestic company, worldwide income is taxable. However, if the entity is treated as a foreign corporation due to the place of effective management (POEM) dispute, only Korean-source income is taxable. For container leasing, Korean-source income from the lease of movable property is determined under Article 93 of the Corporate Tax Act (CITA) and may be subject to final withholding if no permanent establishment exists. Avoid double inclusion of same income under Article 95 and Article 98.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Base and Corporate Tax Rate Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the progressive corporate tax rates to the taxable income. For non-resident shareholders, ensure that the effective tax rate computation does not incorrectly reduce the income subject to withholding tax when the income is repatriated. Straight-line calculation based on Box 3 income after loss carryforward and tax credits.

Claim R&D credits, foreign tax credits, and temporary tax credits under the RSTA. For a container leasing operation, depreciation differences and asset impairment adjustments must be properly documented. Non-resident investors cannot claim personal relief credits; only entity-level credits are permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount Payable / Refund and Withholding Tax Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate final tax payable after eliminating interim tax payments. For a subsidiary of a foreign parent, any dividends paid must be reported in Form No. 24 (withholding tax return) separately. If the entity is a limited company with non-resident directors, their fee income is subject to employment/non-resident personal service withholding; ensure no deduction of domestic tax on international shipping income unless the container leasing activity qualifies as international maritime transport – generally it does not.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax; if return is filed within one month of the statutory deadline, penalty is 10%; additional daily surcharge of 0.022% per day (annual 8.03%) on unpaid tax from the day after the due date to the day of payment; failure to file electronically adds a penalty of KRW 100,000 per return; fraudulent understatement triggers a penalty of 40% of the evaded tax and potential criminal prosecution under Article 118 of the Corporate Tax Act with imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to KRW 100 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (including national income tax 20%) plus local surtax of 10% on the income tax amount, resulting in an effective aggregate rate of 22%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend withholding tax rate under the Korea-foreign jurisdiction DTA (e.g., 5% for 10%+ corporate shareholder, 15% for portfolio), the recipient must submit: (1) an Application for Reduced Withholding Tax Rate (Form No. 36) to the competent tax office before the payment date or within the thereafter stipulated period; (2) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority confirming the beneficial owner status; (3) a Beneficial Ownership Statement confirming the recipient is not a conduit and satisfies the Limitation on Benefits (LOB) clause. Submission via HomeTax or in paper; if received post-payment, refund claims filed under the Framework Act on National Taxes within 3 years of the statutory payment date. Failure to submit results in full 22% withholding and loss of treaty benefit unless a subsequent refund procedure is pursued.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 20% plus local surtax (effective 22%); treaty rates typically 5% (industrial royalties) or 10% (cultural royalties) under most DTAs. Interest: statutory 20% plus local surtax (effective 22%); treaty rate commonly 10% (arm's length interest) or 15% (other interest). Under the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and Korean TP Adjustment Act, interest deductions on excessive thin capital (debt-to-equity ratio > 2:1 for non-financial entities) are disallowed, and the disallowed amount is treated as a constructive dividend subject to 22% withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Comprehensive Local File and Master File mandatory if intercompany transactions exceed KRW 10 billion per year (or KRW 5 billion for transactions with parties in tax havens). Country-by-Country Report required if aggregate group revenue ≥ KRW 300 billion. Penalty for non-submission: up to 3% of the transaction amount and criminal liability for willful omission.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply under the international anti-BEPS framework and the Korean tax reform incorporating the OECD 'Core Income-Generating Activities' (CIGA) test. A container leasing entity must demonstrate that the leasing activities, management decisions, asset maintenance, and risk control functions are actually performed in Korea (or in a qualified foreign jurisdiction) through qualified employees and premises. If the entity is a 'managed holding company' with no substantive local staff, the National Tax Service may recharacterize income as attributable to a foreign permanent establishment or, under the dividend stripping rules, impose 22% withholding on deemed repatriation and deny treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating intermodal container lease rental income by using foreign shell companies to route payments to tax haven jurisdictions, or mischaracterizing lease payments as 'sale proceeds' to avoid corporate income tax and withholding taxes, accompanied by fabricated invoices and loan agreements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act Article 118 (Penal Provisions): imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 100 million; additional 40% evasion penalty on understated tax; for amounts exceeding KRW 1 billion, aggravated punishment up to 10 years imprisonment under Article 18-2 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the Corporate Tax Act and the Commercial Act, directors who knowingly participate in tax evasion are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax plus penalties. The courts can pierce the veil to impose personal liability for the full tax liability. Directors may be blacklisted by the National Tax Service, restricting travel, obtaining government contracts, and financial transactions; criminal conviction results in a criminal record and possible imprisonment, as well as asset seizure to cover unpaid taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Claim of Tax Treaty Benefits / Abuse of DTA
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a reduced withholding tax rate under a Double Tax Agreement using a fraudulent Tax Residency Certificate or a nominee/holding company with no economic substance, when the beneficial owner is a third-country resident. This includes the failure to disclose that the ultimate parent is not a resident of the treaty jurisdiction and the Korean entity's container leases are entirely controlled by a non-resident intermediary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 54-2, abusive treaty claims are denied, and the full 22% withholding tax plus 40% negligence penalty is imposed. The act may also trigger criminal penalties under Article 118 of the Corporate Tax Act for false declarations, and the tax authorities will issue a 'badge of fraud' determination leading to the 10-year statute of limitations (ordinary statute is 5 years).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the false treaty claim are personally liable for the additional tax and penalties. Under the ‘piercing the corporate veil’ doctrine, a director may be held criminally liable for fraud, and the court may order restitution plus unpaid taxes. Travel bans (blacklisting) and entry restriction to all OECD member states are possible after Interpol red notice for cross-border tax fraud; imprisonment up to 5 years is commonly applied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: File Fabrication and False Accounting (AML Integration)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating dual books of account: one showing actual container lease rentals to foreign clients, and a second understating revenues to evade tax; simultaneously using the company’s bank account to launder the unreported proceeds by layering through Swift wire transfers and ACH debits to offshore accounts under the guise of 'management fees' or 'intercompany settlement'.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes imposes imprisonment of 1 year to life (up to life for amounts ≥ KRW 5 billion) and fines of up to 5 times the laundered amount. Under Article 102 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, illegal cross-border transfers result in penalties up to 70% of the transferred amount. The National Tax Service will impose the 40% perjury penalty and also report to the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) under the Specialized Financial Supervision Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are individually liable for money laundering offenses; the corporate veil is pierced because the company is the instrument of crime. Personal assets can be seized at the criminal confiscation stage. Directors face a mandatory travel ban, entry to South Korea and treaty partners is restricted, and personal criminal liability includes imprisonment from 3 to 10 years, with a life sentence possible for aggravated amounts. The Financial Supervisory Service can also impose a lifetime business restriction on the director from serving as a corporate officer in any financial or leasing business.
